LIGHTING (CRITICAL for realism):

This is photorealistic creature photography on a black studio backdrop, shot like a hero portrait for a film. Cinematic three-point lighting setup, NOT flat AI render.

KEY LIGHT:
- Hard cinematic key from upper-left, ~45° above and ~30° to the side
- Strong but softened — like a large softbox at distance, not a bare bulb
- Slightly warm (3200-4000K) — gives red flesh and bone shield warmth and depth
- Casts directional shadows: under the right side of the jaw, under rib segments, between spikes, in shield grooves
- Defines underlying form

FILL LIGHT:
- Cool subtle fill from the right at low intensity (1/4 of key)
- Slight blue-gray (5500-6500K) — gives shadow detail without flattening
- Critical for skin subsurface to read on the shadow side

RIM / EDGE LIGHTS:
- WARM RED rim from below and behind, low intensity but visible
- Catches back edges of the bone shield, spine spikes, back of head — silhouette gets faint inner glow, body emits subtle heat from within
- Separate COLD rim from above-behind catches metal spike tips and steel half of sword-arm — small bright cold highlights pricking the silhouette
- Body hair catches rim lights — soft fuzz outline visible against the black background

CONTACT SHADOW: soft contact shadow on the gray ground plane, diffused/ambient occlusion style, not a hard cast shadow.

PRINCIPLES:
- Cinematic three-point with cinematic falloff — NOT flat product lighting
- Specular hits on metal are the BRIGHTEST points in frame
- Deepest shadows in spike clusters and shield grooves are nearly pure black but never fully crushed
- Subsurface scattering visible at thin flesh areas
- Lighting must reveal a FOUR-MATERIAL creature: soft pink flesh + hard red bone shield + cold dark steel + matte charred carbon — each reads differently under the same light
